sense: the way the parts of something are arranged

evidence: Cic. N.D. 1.47: conpositiō membrōrum, the edition’s spelling
Cic. Off. 1.127: hanc nātūrae tam dīligentem fabricam
Cic. Brut. 33: verbōrum quasi strūctūra (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In Cicero only as a figure, with quasi; freely in later prose (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quae conpositiō membrōrum, quae cōnfōrmātiō līniāmentōrum, quae figūra, quae speciēs hūmāna potest esse pulchrior?
phrases.english: what structure of limbs, what shape of features, what figure or appearance could be more beautiful than the human?

phrases.latin: hanc nātūrae tam dīligentem fabricam imitāta est hominum verēcundia
phrases.english: this careful design of nature has been copied by human modesty

phrases.latin: nihil esse pulchrius in omnī ratiōne vītae dispositiōne atque ōrdine
phrases.english: that in every walk of life nothing is finer than arrangement and order

sources: Lewis & Short: compositio · Lewis & Short: fabrica · Lewis & Short: structura · Lewis & Short: conformatio · Lewis & Short: ordo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. organize: structure.

Cicero, De natura deorum 1 and De officiis 1, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026). Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cato (Columella)), checked against the editions named there.
